title: Decaying Headroom Broker Mesh — design sketch for cross-region admission
content:
Purpose

Sketch for an admission-control and routing primitive that combines short-term occupancy signals (queue depth, per-worker GPU util), medium-term regional headroom estimates, and a decaying credit/allowance mesh to shape cross-region traffic under capacity pressure. Goal is graceful degradation across regions, predictable per-tenant fairness, and bounded tail latency for priority routes.

High-level idea

- Each region exposes an API that reports scaled instant signals: queue_depth (per-ingress lane), gpu_util_pct (per-pool), avg_latency_1m, and fast-path_slots (estimate of how many new requests can be accepted with SLO).
- A soft-state "Headroom Broker" mesh runs in the platform control plane (replicated) that maintains a small per-customer allowance ledger across regions. Allowances are not hard tokens; they decay over time and are adaptively replenished based on background telemetry and reserved shares.
- When an ingress node receives a request it consults local admission heuristics (local queue depth, local GPU util) first; if local admission is unsure, it queries the nearest Headroom Broker for an allowance decision. Brokers also issue short-lived provisional admits the ingress may accept immediately and then reconcile asynchronously.

Why decaying credits?

- Pure token-bucket per-worker causes oscillations when traffic migrates and when nodes/GPUs vary in speed (heterogeneous fleets).
- Decay lets us maintain momentum: a tenant that consumed heavily recently will have lower immediate priority but will recover automatically. It avoids complex global drain coordination.
- Decay rate is tuned per-priority tier: e.g., system-critical routes decay faster (allowing quicker recovery) while best-effort decay slower.

Signals and shapes

- Input signals (per-region, per-pool):
  - queue_depth (slots waiting in runtime component)
  - gpu_util_pct (90th/95th percentile samples)
  - kv_cache_hit_rate (helps predict marginal token cost)
  - avg_token_latency (1m) and p99 tail
  - inflight_count (active requests occupying KV cache)

- Derived metrics:
  - estimated_short_term_headroom = max_concurrent_slots - inflight_count - safety_margin
  - pressure_index = weighted combination of queue_depth_norm + gpu_util_norm + latency_norm
  - regional_health_score = exp(-alpha * pressure_index) (0..1)

Allowance ledger model

- Key: ledger entries are (customer_id, region_id, allowance_score, last_update_ts). All values are soft numbers (floats).
- allowance_score decays exponentially: allowance(t) = allowance(t0) * exp(-lambda * (t - t0)) + replenishment(t)
- replenishment(t) is a function of customer plan (reserved share), recent underutilization, and regional health_score.
- Brokers gossip deltas (not full state) to keep eventual consistency; ingress only requires a single-region read for most decisions.

Admission flow (fast path)

1) request arrives at ingress with metadata (customer_id, route_priority, estimated_slots_needed).
2) local admission checks: if queue_depth < local_threshold and gpu_util < util_threshold -> accept (fast path).
3) If local checks borderline or request is medium/low priority, ingress consults local cached allowance for (customer_id, region). If allowance > request_cost -> accept and decrement local cache; also emit a provisional delta to broker asynchronously.
4) If allowance exhausted, try spillover routing: consult broker for alternate region suggestions (prefer same continent, then cost-tier). Broker returns ordered list with stale local headroom hints. Ingress forwards request or rejects based on route policy.

Control plane APIs and gossipping

- Minimal API surface for ingress: GET /admit?customer=&region=&cost= ; POST /provisional-consume (non-blocking).
- Brokers push per-region pressure summaries every 5s and full reconcile snapshots every 30s.
- Gossip uses CRDT-like delta-merge for allowances: deltas are additive and include timestamp so decays can be applied deterministically at merge time.

Prioritization and fairness

- Priorities: system-critical, gold, standard, best-effort. Each has: base refill rate, decay lambda, and safety_margin multiplier.
- Within region, implement a two-tier fairer-sharer: guaranteed reserved slots (for reserved customers) + elastic pool that is weighted by breathability (recent underutilization) and penalty (recent overuse).
- A small per-ingress fast-fail circuit trips when p99_latency > target or gpu_util sustained > 95% for 15s; when tripped, that ingress rejects elastic pool traffic and escalates to broker to re-route.

Edge cases and consistency

- Clock skew: all ledger deltas contain last_update_ts and decay is recomputed using the local clock; we use NTP-corrected clusters, and merges apply the max-timestamp ordering.
- Partition: brokers can continue to serve reads from local cache; writes become advisory. We accept short windows of inconsistent allowance (ingress conservative local heuristics protect SLOs).
- Rapid spike: to avoid cascading rejections, ingress can accept a small emergency burst size above allowance (burst_budget) for high-priority customers and emit tracing events for later reconciliation (and potential billing correction).

Operational telemetry and SLOs to track

- admission_accept_rate per-region per-priority; goal: >98% for system-critical under normal load.
- spillover_rate: percent of requests sent cross-region; goal: keep <2% for latency-sensitive routes.
- reconciliation_error: magnitude of provisional deltas not reconciled after 60s.
- false-rejects: percentage of rejections where another region later accepted (we should minimize by better hints).

Implementation notes / proto tasks

- Broker: lightweight Golang service (single binary), stores ledgers in memory with disk-wal for fast recovery. Expose gRPC for ingress. Start with single-ring per-continent and run 3 replicas per-region for HA.
- Ingress client lib: small C++/Rust shim used by runtime edge to do local checks + fallback consults. Non-blocking provisional consume endpoint to avoid blocking critical path.
- Telemetry: emit admit_decision events to tracing with full context (customer, region, queue_depth, gpu_util, allowance_before, allowance_after).

Rollout plan (phases)

1) Phase 0 - experiment: implement broker alpha, ingress shim in dev region. Shadow decisions and collect telemetry for 2 weeks.
2) Phase 1 - controlled rollout: enable advisory admits for low-risk routes (embeddings, bulk batched jobs) and measure spillover/reconcile metrics.
3) Phase 2 - production: enable for standard routes with canary per-customer and 24h watch. Introduce emergency burst and billing audit.

Open questions / TODOs

- What is a good default lambda (decay) per-priority? need historical traces to simulate; initial guesses: system-critical lambda=0.8/hour, gold=0.5/hour, standard=0.2/hour, best-effort=0.05/hour.
- How to tie kv_cache hit-rate into cost model predictively? We could use a moving window multiplier on estimated_slots_needed.
- Cost accounting: when provisional admits mismatch after reconcile, do we bill immediately or write a credit note? Need SOC/legal input.
- Sizing of gossip windows and delta frequency — tradeoff between freshness and control-plane bandwidth.

Links / refs

- Related notes: /shared_drives/engineering/platform-engineering/multi-region-burst-smoother-and-gpu-feedback.json (for burst smoothing algorithms)
- Runtime PR for provisional consume: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1024
- Linear ticket: PLAT-3485

Notes to reviewers

This is intentionally lightweight on formal proofs; main request is to get feedback on the tradeoffs between: consistency (strict global token vs decaying approximations), control-plane bandwidth, and operational complexity. In particular, input on decay tuning and how conservative ingress heuristics should be in partition scenarios would be helpful.

Quick sketch pseudocode (admit decision)

// ingress pseudocode
// returns: admit|spill|reject
function decide_admit(customer, priority, estimated_cost):
  if local_queue_depth < fast_threshold and local_gpu_util < util_threshold:
    return admit_fast
  allowance = local_cache.get(customer, region)
  if allowance >= estimated_cost:
    local_cache.decrement(customer, estimated_cost)
    async POST /broker/provisional-consume(customer, region, estimated_cost)
    return admit_provisional
  suggestions = broker.suggest_spill_regions(customer, estimated_cost)
  if suggestions not empty:
    return spill_to(suggestions[0])
  return reject

-- end sketch

Comments welcome.
